desc: Establish basic invariants: occupied-square count cannot increase, the position map is monotone, and merged pieces never split.
Derive radius feasibility for monotone surjective consecutive-block assignments using source-gap boundary constraints.
Implement the current exact candidate fixed-k DP and confirm it passes all public samples.
Disprove earliest-feasible greedy boundary parity optimality; counterexample N=3, A=111, B=110 has answer 1 while the earlier greedy code outputs 2.
Characterize exactly which monotone non-expanding maps are compositions of k pull maps, including parity, center-hit capacity, and endpoint restrictions.
Derive and prove the exact fixed-k feasibility criterion jointly covering distance, source-gap boundaries, and parity counts.

Derive a provably O(N log N) (or amortized O(N)) compressed DP/data structure for the exact fixed-k boundary-chain feasibility test, preserving both minimum and maximum parity-mismatch counts without enumerating every boundary interval pair.
Turn exact fixed-k feasibility into a minimum-operation algorithm with linear or near-linear total complexity.
Exhaustively validate the fixed-k characterization and parity condition against enumerated pull-center sequences for small N.
Validate the final algorithm on samples, one-piece cases, all-target-occupied cases, adjacent pieces, gaps, endpoint centers, and adversarial alternative block assignments.
Implement the final Python solution with buffered input/output.
